description: Hydrogen is a chemical element with the symbol H and atomic number 1. It is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, constituting about 75% of all normal matter. Under standard conditions, hydrogen is a gas of diatomic molecules with the formula H2, called dihydrogen, which is colorless, odorless, non-toxic, and highly combustible.
uses: Hydrogen's main industrial uses include fossil fuel processing and ammonia production for fertilizer. It is also used in nuclear fusion, as a tracer in isotope geochemistry, and in specialized self-powered lighting devices. Emerging uses for hydrogen include the use of fuel cells to generate electricity.
characteristics: Dihydrogen is colorless, odorless, non-toxic, and highly flammable, reacting with oxygen to produce liquid water and releasing 286 kilojoules of heat per mole. Hydrogen gas forms explosive mixtures with air in concentrations from 4% to 74% and has an autoignition temperature of 500 °C. Hydrogen flames emit faint blue and ultraviolet light.
